reason: The goal and introduction point toward seeds spreading across the post-ice-age world.
expectation: Seed dispersal should help new growth spread through the world.

alternatives.reason: Planting seeds could start growth, but dispersal seems more directly tied to growth beyond view.

effect: Seed dispersal has no available operation now, so I need another route to spreading growth.
reason: Seeds and soil previously produced green shoots, making this a grounded next attempt.
expectation: Seeds in soil should produce green shoots or another beginning of growth.

alternatives.reason: Inspecting the world could reveal which available item acts there.

effect: Seeds combine with seasons to make dormant seeds, suggesting growth may resume when conditions change.
reaction: The seasonal pause is a useful surprise after the failed planting attempt.
reason: Dormant seeds may respond to another change of seasons, but their available partners are not yet clear.
expectation: Inspection should reveal how the seeds can resume growth or spread.

alternatives.reason: Soil could support eventual growth, but dormancy may require another step first.

effect: Dormant seeds combined with seed dispersal to make scattered seeds, bringing the spreading route back into play.
reaction: The automatic combination made the next step clear.
reason: Scattered seeds may now take root in soil, though their available partners are still uncertain.
expectation: The scattered seeds should establish new growth in the soil.

alternatives.reason: Inspection could reveal their available partner before attempting to plant them.

effect: The scattered seeds took root in soil and became a young grove.
reaction: It is satisfying to see the seeds establish growth after dispersal.
reason: The young grove seems ready to become part of the world after the ice.
expectation: The grove will spread or continue growing in the recovering world.

effect: The young grove became a forest beyond the horizon, completing the goal and showing growth and decomposition continuing without my intervention.
reaction: The open-ended image was a satisfying conclusion to the seed's journey.

mostWorthwhile.text: Growing scattered seeds into a grove and then a forest made the handoff from deliberate placement to an independently continuing world tangible.

leastWorthwhile.text: The first attempt was frustrating: seed dispersal sounded directly relevant to the goal, but it had no available operation yet.

surprise.text: Seeds needed a seasonal period of dormancy before dispersal became available; the description also clarified that dormancy does not guarantee survival.

arbitrary.text: The need to combine seeds with seasons before dispersing them was not obvious from the goal, even though dormancy itself had a clear purpose once explained.

continue.text: Yes. The conclusion made me curious about how the world would change without direct control, although the completed chapter feels like a natural stopping point.
